en: Jose Rizal annotated Antonio de Morga’s historical book to prove Filipinos already had a rich, complex culture before the Spanish colonized the islands.
The Philippine Supreme Court can declare a law unconstitutional, but it requires a vote of at least eight out of its fifteen justices to do so.
The narra was declared the national tree in 1934 because its extremely hard, durable wood was historically used to build Spanish galleons and grand houses.
If the ancient Ifugao rice terraces were laid end to end, they would stretch halfway around the entire globe.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the first two-way radiotelephone in 1938, predating modern cellular communication technology by several decades.
Before the Spanish arrived, Filipinos wrote on bamboo and leaves using Baybayin, an ancient alphabetic script where each character represents a full syllable.
During the Lucban Pahiyas Festival, locals decorate their houses with kiping, which are colorful, leaf-shaped wafers made from ground rice.
Marcela Agoncillo and her daughters hand-sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong before it was unfurled during the 1898 independence proclamation.
The Sangguniang Kabataan allows elected Filipino youth officials, aged fifteen to seventeen, to draft local legislation and manage community youth budgets.
The traditional Filipino value of bayanihan originated from the physical practice of an entire community carrying a nipa hut to a new location.
Fernando Amorsolo, the first National Artist for Painting, is famous for his unique backlighting technique that captures the golden glow of rural Philippine sunlight.
Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista authored and personally read the original 1898 Act of Declaration of Independence in Spanish to a massive crowd in Kawit, Cavite.
